thread.title: Markets Now: Dow Gains 85 Points as No News is Good News - Barron's

author: Ben Levisohn
title: Markets Now: Dow Gains 85 Points as No News is Good News - Barron's
text:
By Ben Levisohn Updated June 7, 2018 11:01 a.m. ET Want to know why the Dow Jones Industrial Average is doing what it's doing? Check back here for a semi-live look at the volatile markets from Barron's reporters.
Illustration: Bloomberg News 10:45 a.m. If you just look at the Dow Jones Industrial Average , you'd think it was just a regular ho-hum day on Wall Street . The blue-chip benchmark is, after all, up 90.22 points, or 0.4%, at 25,236.61. The S&P 500 , however, is off 0.1% at 2770.04, and the Nasdaq Composite is off 0.7% 7633.83.
No surprise there. The Dow is price-weighted, so a stock like McDonald's (MCD), which is up 3.2% at $167.57, carries nearly as much weight as the tech giants. That's good news on a day like today when the Faanmgss are getting hit.
Facebook (FB) has fallen 2.3% to $186.95, Apple (AAPL) has declined 0.6% to $192.73, Amazon.com (AMZN) is off 0.9% at $1,679.94, Microsoft (MSFT) has slipped 1.3% to $101.11, Netflix (NFLX) has dropped 2.3% to $358.91, and Alphabet (GOOGL), aka Google, is down 1.7% to $1,127.42.
Should we be worried? Probably not yet. Yesterday we observed that the tech sector was getting mighty oversold , and that's often, though not always, led to a short-term pullback. Don't be surprised if tech's weakness last s for a few more days.
7:40 a.m. With no real news this morning, the market looks set for a repeat of yesterday . Dow Jones Industrial Average futures have risen 60 points, or 0.2%, while Nasdaq Composite futures have declined 0.04%, as tech appears set to lag again. S&P 500 futures have ticked up 0.1%.
"The Dow Jones broke above the 25,000-points threshold ...and given the positive bias in the markets the next level for the US benchmark index should be around the 25,600 points' area where the February highs are found," writes Konstantinos Anthis , head of research at ADS Securities .
Up, up and away?
